records.name: Agape Center for Healing Arts
records.summary: A healing arts group that holds retreats on healing, art and care for the earth. It lists a Philadelphia address and runs an online community on Discord.
records.what_you_do: Join the online Discord community through the invite on the website, or email the group to ask about its next retreat. The site describes retreats, art therapy, healing movement, and free or low-cost community programs.

schedule.text: Retreats are held from time to time, not on a set schedule. No upcoming dates are posted.

cost.text: Donations start at any amount. The site does not post retreat prices.

first_step.how: Join the Discord community through the invite on agapehealing.center, or email the group to ask how to take part in the next retreat.
first_step.basis: Anyone can join the public Discord through the invite on the website, which is a clear way in. The site does not describe how to sign up for a retreat, and it says gifts of $1,000 or more come with a retreat spot.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not walk a first timer through a visit. Its retreats combine healing arts, movement, and ecological learning, and the group describes its approach as spiritual but non-sectarian. The site does not post how long retreats run, how many people attend, or what they cost.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before you plan a trip, since no upcoming dates are posted.

records.notes: The site has no join or volunteer pages. The retreat list shows no 2026 dates. Past retreats were in Brazil and at Pendle Hill (Pennsylvania, outside the city), and the Philadelphia address is the base. The verdict is publish, but a reviewer may prefer out_of_area. The vision page mentions sliding-scale fees and scholarships only as fundraising goals, so no retreat price is recorded. A course link on the vision page looked broken. The July 2025 retreat date moved out of schedule.text and stays in last_sign_of_life.

records.name: AHARI (A Home Is A Right)
records.summary: Helps veterans and their families with housing and support services. It runs a yearly Veteran Stand Down, where community volunteers help alongside government agencies and nonprofits.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the Veteran Stand Down, which offers screenings, legal help, meals, and referrals to veterans. Veterans who need help can start on the Services page. The group also takes donations and sponsorships.

schedule.text: The Veteran Stand Down is held once a year. No date for a future Stand Down is posted.

locations.label: Philadelphia Convention Center, Hall B (2026 Stand Down site)

first_step.how: Email ahari.at.work@gmail.com, or send a General Inquiry through the Send a Message form on the Contact Us page, to ask how to volunteer at the next Veteran Stand Down.
first_step.basis: The 2026 Stand Down sign-up was posted, but that date has passed and the site lists no later date or volunteer steps, so the way in is unclear beyond contacting the office.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 2026 event was set for 10 am to 6:30 pm at the Philadelphia Convention Center, with screenings, legal and benefits help, meals, clothing, and referrals for veterans. The site does not list specific volunteer roles, so ask which jobs need help before you come.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email about volunteer roles and arrival time, since the site does not post them.

records.notes: The Stand Down page still shows the 2026 event as upcoming with a register button, but its date (September 12, 2026) had passed at this check. The sign-up leads to an outside registration page, which was not opened. The home page Volunteer button goes to Contact Us. The site gives no volunteer roles, office hours or phone number. Tier 1 said the Stand Down was upcoming with no date, and its first step is replaced for that reason.

records.name: Al-Aqsa Islamic Society
records.summary: A mosque and community center in Kensington with a Youth Club, an Interfaith program and an Outreach program. The society has been operating since 1989.
records.what_you_do: Kids ages 7 to 16 can join the Youth Club for service projects, art and trips. The Outreach program works with partners on arts, service and planting projects, including free mural workshops open to the public. The Interfaith program has helped host the Interfaith Peacewalk for about 20 years.

schedule.text: Youth Club meets on club days, but the days and times are not posted. The events calendar had no items when checked, so ask the office for current times.

cost.text: The site does not state fees for the Youth Club or the Interfaith program. Mural Arts workshops are described as free.

access.notes: The conference room used for elections is wheelchair accessible, and parking is available, according to the Outreach page. The site gives no other accessibility details.

first_step.how: Call the mosque at (215) 765-2743 to ask about joining. For the Youth Club, call the youth coordinator at (215) 765-0607 and ask about open spots, since spaces are limited.
first_step.basis: The free mural workshops are open to the public, and the Youth Club has a named coordinator to contact. Youth Club spots are limited, and the site does not describe visitor steps for the other programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: For kids, the Youth Club mixes service projects, such as making care packages and visiting senior homes, with art and fun activities. Parents are invited to help on trips and service days. The Peacewalk provides shuttle buses, so walkers can park and ride to the start.
first_visit_tips: Parking is available, according to the Outreach page.
Call ahead, since the site does not post program times or visiting hours.

records.notes: Youth Club days and times are not posted. The youth coordinator's email uses another organization's domain (arabamericancdc.org), so it was not recorded. The events calendar and news page have no dated items, so no last sign of life is recorded and status stays probably_active. Prayer times were not in the text the fetch could read. The Peacewalk and Mural Arts are in leads_only.

records.name: Alcoholics Anonymous Southeastern Pennsylvania Intergroup Association
records.summary: The local service office for Alcoholics Anonymous groups in five southeastern Pennsylvania counties, Philadelphia included. Volunteer members answer a 24-hour help line and help newcomers find a meeting.
records.what_you_do: Call the 24-hour help line to talk with a local member, or use the meeting finder to pick a meeting. Members can also take service roles, such as committee and 12-step volunteer work.

schedule.text: The help line answers 24 hours a day, every day. Meeting times vary by group, so check the meeting finder for each one.

cost.text: Free to attend. AA is supported by member contributions.

access.notes: The site links to Deaf and ASL-interpreted meetings and to an online meeting list. A Spanish-language helpline is listed, but the site shows two different numbers for it, so confirm the number before you call.

first_step.how: Call the 24-hour help line at 215-923-7900, or find a beginners' meeting in the meeting finder and go to see what it is like.
first_step.basis: The site runs a beginners' meeting finder and a 12-Step Call that connects newcomers with a local member, and newcomers may attend meetings for free without having to share.
first_step.what_to_expect: Newcomers can attend meetings for free and listen without speaking. If you want to share, you may tell your own story or read from AA literature, and nothing is required. The site does not say how long meetings last or how many people attend.
first_visit_tips: Check the meeting finder for the address, format and time before you go, since times vary by group.
If you would like to talk first, call the help line to speak with a local member.

records.notes: The site shows 215-923-7900 as the 24-hour English line and, in one place, as the Spanish line. Most places list 215-398-2540 for Spanish, so confirm before publishing. The beginners' meeting finder showed no meetings in the text the fetch could read, so its list may load by script. The Deaf and ASL directory link on the site returned 404 at check, so it is not used as a source. Office hours are not posted, and the office shares the help line number. The 2026 Gratitude Breakfast (September 27, 2026) is the newest dated item and had passed at check. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life was just the year and is now a month.

records.name: Pennsylvania Fibershed
records.summary: A group working to make Pennsylvania's fiber and textile trade fairer and more sustainable. It connects fiber growers, makers and businesses, runs a book club, and hosts the Philly Fiber Fest.
records.what_you_do: Join the online book club, come to Philly Fiber Fest to shop, learn and meet makers, volunteer on research, admin, events, social media or marketing through a form on the site, or become a member.

schedule.text: The online book club meets for about an hour and picks new books regularly. The page does not post a meeting schedule.

locations.label: Philly Fiber Fest venue (Village of Industry & Art)

cost.text: The book club page lists no fee. Individual membership is $72 a year or $10 a month. Fest visitor prices are not posted yet.

access.notes: The Fest has a sensory-friendly space with calming natural textures, and a Kids' Corner with hands-on fiber crafts. The Fest page does not describe wheelchair access or parking.

first_step.how: Sign up for the book club through the Join here form on the book club page, and sign up for updates through the Fest page to hear when visitor tickets open.
first_step.basis: The book club is open to anyone who fills in its sign-up form, the Fest is open to visitors, and there is a mailing list. The site does not say whether one book club session is a fine first step.
first_step.what_to_expect: The book club meets online for about an hour and talks about each pick. The Fest is a one day fair with more than 30 vendors, a fiber art show, demonstrations, and optional paid workshops. Visitor tickets are not posted yet, so check the Fest page before the day.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for event updates, since visitor tickets are not posted yet.
Ask by email about parking and transit, since the Fest page does not mention them.

records.notes: Visitor tickets and Fest parking are not posted yet. The vendor application closed September 25, 2026. The Weaving Circle co-presents the Fest and is in leads_only. The home page newsletter form says its storage still needs setup, so the mailing list may not work (not tested). Membership is separate from the book club, and the page does not say membership is needed for either event. The volunteer form was not visible in the text read. Dated events moved out of schedule.text and the newest event date is in last_sign_of_life.

records.name: Almanac Projects
records.summary: A dance, circus and theater company in Philadelphia. It makes shows, offers free Helpful Hints workshops, and runs AlmanAcro, an open acrobatics class on Monday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Take the open AlmanAcro acrobatics class on Monday evenings, join a free Helpful Hints workshop, buy a show ticket, or offer behind the scenes help such as stage management or production work.

schedule.text: AlmanAcro, the open ensemble acrobatics class, meets every Monday at 6:30 pm for 2 hours at Acro& in Northern Liberties. Helpful Hints workshops are scheduled separately, so check the calendar.

locations.label: Helpful Hints workshops (Pig Iron Theatre Company, Studio A)

cost.text: Helpful Hints workshops are free. AlmanAcro is $30 a session at full price, with a sliding scale.

requirements.gear: Clothes you can move in, and a water bottle, for the AlmanAcro class.

access.notes: The AlmanAcro studio is up a flight of stairs and is not ADA accessible, according to its class page. The site does not describe access to the Pig Iron workshop room.

first_step.how: Book a session of AlmanAcro through the Book a session link on its page, or fill in the Airtable sign-up form on the Almanac site to join a free Helpful Hints workshop.
first_step.basis: AlmanAcro is open to everyone and you book online. The free workshops are open to the public with a sign-up form. The class page does not say the class is for beginners.
first_step.what_to_expect: AlmanAcro runs for two hours and starts with a warm-up, then skill practice, partner and group work, open training, and a short group creative exercise. It is aimed at performers who want to learn bases, flying and tumbling, and at acrobats who want more ease with performing and improvising. The Helpful Hints workshops are free sessions that pair older and younger people to build short duets together.
first_visit_tips: Wear clothes you can move in, and bring a water bottle.
The AlmanAcro studio is up stairs, so plan ahead if you need step-free access.
Confirm the room when you sign up for a Helpful Hints workshop, since the site does not list the room.

records.notes: AlmanAcro is run by Almanac Projects and is linked from the site header. The Pig Iron street address comes from a public charity listing (Benevity). The room called Studio A is not confirmed on any page checked, and the company's own address pages returned 404. The November 7, 2026 workshop is at The Ginkgo Center, a venue, so it is not listed as a lead. One-time show prices are left out of cost. The tier 1 phrase about running festivals was not seen on the site and was removed.

records.name: Alzheimer's Association Delaware Valley Chapter: Caregiver Support Groups
records.summary: Free groups for unpaid family members and friends who care for someone with Alzheimer's or another dementia. Trained facilitators lead them by phone, video or in person.
records.what_you_do: Talk through the hard parts of caregiving, get practical tips, and hear from others in a similar spot. The chapter also runs early-stage groups for people with a diagnosis, and it offers ALZConnected, a free online community for people with dementia and their caregivers.

schedule.text: Group times vary and change, so call the helpline or search the group finder to confirm the day, time and place before you go.

cost.text: Free. All services and resources are free.

access.notes: Phone and video groups are offered alongside in-person groups. The helpline offers help in more than 200 languages, and the site has a Spanish version, but the group pages are in English.

first_step.how: Call the 24/7 helpline at 800.272.3900, or use the find a support group search on alz.org, then call the group's contact to confirm its next date.
first_step.basis: Open to any unpaid caregiver, free to join, with a 24/7 helpline and a group finder. Early-stage groups need a diagnosis and a prescreening call first.
first_step.what_to_expect: A trained facilitator leads each group, which can meet by phone, by video, or in person. Caregiver groups are for unpaid family members and friends, not paid caregivers. Early-stage groups are for people with a doctor's diagnosis and require a prescreening before you join.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead to confirm the day, time and format, since group details change.
Ask about phone or video options if travel is hard.

records.notes: Two chapter pages were read: the record URL (alz.org/delval/support) and alz.org/sepa/support, which is labeled as the Southeastern Pennsylvania chapter. Confirm the chapter name before publishing. The tier 1 claim about younger-onset groups was not found on either page and was removed. The group finder could not be read, so no Philadelphia meeting listings were checked. The autumn donation banner is not evidence about groups and was not used.

leads_only.name: Interfaith Peacewalk for Peace and Reconciliation of Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Peace walk that Al-Aqsa has hosted or joined for about 20 years, with shuttle buses and a shared meal at the end. The page gives an email contact but no website of its own. Not checked further.

leads_only.name: The Weaving Circle
leads_only.note: Co-presents Philly Fiber Fest with Pennsylvania Fibershed, per the Fest page. No website link is given. Not checked.

leads_only.name: Mural Arts Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Named on Al-Aqsa's Outreach page as the provider of free mural workshops. Its home page shows a city-wide public art group with education and restorative justice programs. Workshop details were not on the home page, so its programs page needs checking.

blocked.note: Deaf and ASL AA directory linked from the SEPIA site; not found at check. Dropped as a lead.
Company address page not found at check.
Studio rentals page not found at check.

notes: Searches: 1 (Pig Iron address, used only for the public building address). Fetches: 37. All seven groups received deep pages (3 to 6 fetches each) and the budget was not exhausted. Corrections to tier 1: (1) AHARI Stand Down date of September 12, 2026 has passed, so the first step changed. (2) AA last_sign_of_life changed from a bare year to 2026-09. (3) Alzheimer's younger-onset claim removed. (4) Almanac cost no longer carries a one-time show price, and the festivals claim was removed. (5) Fibershed Fest dates moved out of schedule.text. (6) Agape schedule.text no longer carries the July 2025 date. Venues not turned into leads: Pig Iron Theatre Company (workshop venue, company address pages 404), The Ginkgo Center (November 7 workshop venue), Acro&, Village of Industry & Art, and Philadelphia Convention Center. Aqsa Academy (aqsaacademy.org) is a tuition school with enrollment for 2026 to 2027, not a community group, so it is dropped. Mural Arts is kept in leads_only as a partner, although the fetch shows it is a large institution, so the common rule to turn fetched leads into records or drop them with reasons is in tension with the tier 2 brief. Reviewer: Agape verdict is publish with low confidence, since most listed activity is outside Philadelphia.
